limitations: The printed Appendix G proof is erroneous even though the intended theorem is recoverable.
The fixed-function and positive-denominator conditions are mathematically necessary but left implicit in the paper.
The absolute constant 16 is a valid conservative certificate, not an optimized constant.
The 1024-run stress suite is diagnostic and is not presented as the proof.

negative_controls.reason: the empirical conditional mean and Eq. 9 are undefined
invalidates both effective-count and target-mass reductions
it introduces sqrt(K) and omits target-mass estimation; the corrected proof uses a Hilbert-space bound

concentration_reference.citation: Pinelis (1994), Optimum Bounds for the Distributions of Martingales in Banach Spaces
concentration_reference.role: dimension-free Bernstein-type control for bounded sums in 2-smooth/Hilbert spaces

proof.constant_budget: The two conditional-mean terms cost 8*sqrt(2); target-mass fluctuation costs at most 4; total <16. Since log(2BK/delta) dominates the union logs for K>=2, Eq. 9 holds with the absolute constant C=16.
proof.sample_complexity: For balanced positive counts N_dj proportional to N_d/B, the radius is O(sqrt(B log(2BK/delta)/N)); hence N=O(B log(2BK/delta)/epsilon^2), or O(B/epsilon^2) with logarithmic confidence/class factors suppressed.
proof.self_normalized_vector_lemma: Hilbert-space Bernstein applied to sum a_j(p-mu_j), together with scalar Bernstein for N_j, yields ||muhat_j-mu_j|| <= 8 sqrt(log(4B/delta)/N_j). If N_j<16 log(4B/delta), the same inequality follows from the simplex diameter sqrt(2).
proof.setup: For assignment a_j(X) in [0,1], define q_j=E[a_j], mu_j=E[a_j p(X)]/q_j, N_j=sum_i a_j(X_i), and muhat_j=sum_i a_j(X_i)p(X_i)/N_j.
proof.target_identity: For strictly positive soft counts, sum_j what_j/N_tj=B/N_t exactly.
proof.target_mass: The assignment vector lies in the B-simplex. E||what-q_t||_1 <= sqrt(B/N_t); bounded differences adds sqrt(2 log(1/delta)/N_t). Multiplication by the maximum two-domain simplex-mean distance sqrt(2) is absorbed by the target B/N_t term already present in Eq. 9.
proof.union: Apply the lemma to source and target for all B bins.
proof.weighted_contraction: For target empirical weights what_j=N_tj/N_t and sum_j what_j=1, sum_j what_j/sqrt(N_dj) <= sqrt(sum_j what_j/N_dj).

scope.classes: K>=2, posterior vectors in the K-simplex
scope.counts: positive realized source and target soft counts for every included bin
scope.domains: iid source and target evaluation samples
scope.functions: posterior and simplex-valued hard/soft assignment maps fixed independently of evaluation samples
scope.strength: absolute error bound, stronger than the paper's displayed one-sided difference
